source: Public API of the Objective-C headers at 1fddee2 (2026-11-12), the commit before the Swift migration began; generated once from those headers (with the comments of scripts/harmonyos-api-map.py). The Public API rule forbids removing any of these symbols. Later public symbols whose declarations moved into Swift are appended (2026-11-13: -cyl_moveBadgeToCurrentTabButtonIfNeeded).

symbols.name: CYLBadgeAppearance
symbols.comment: App-wide default badge style. Most apps use the same badge everywhere (a red background, white text, one font, the same corner offset), but each badge property belongs to one object, so it had to be set on every tab, bar button and view again. Set the defaults here once, typically in `-application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:`, before showing badges: CYLBadgeAppearance *appearance = [CYLBadgeAppearance globalAppearance]; appearance.backgroundColor = [UIColor systemPinkColor]; appearance.font = [UIFont boldSystemFontOfSize:10]; appearance.centerOffset = CGPointMake(-2, 2); Precedence: a value set on an object (e.g. `viewController.cyl_badgeBackgroundColor`) wins over the global one; the global one wins over the built-in default. This covers every badge host: UIViewController, UITabBarItem, UIBarButtonItem, UIControl and UIView. Badges created later use the new defaults. A badge already on screen picks up new colors, font and border the next time it is shown (`-cyl_showBadgeValue:animationType:`); a red dot keeps its size and position until its style changes. So set the appearance before showing badges. Use it on the main thread, like the rest of UIKit.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarMinimizeBehavior
symbols.comment: How the tab bar reacts to scrolling (issue #13). One value for every style, set with `-[CYLTabBarController cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior]`: - Liquid Glass (iOS 26+): passed to the native `UITabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior`; the system minimizes (shrinks) the tab bar, and the plus button is centered on its tab meanwhile. - FlatDesign: the tab bar is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` while the current page scrolls. - Classic tab bar (iOS 25 and earlier, and iOS 26 in UI compatibility mode): the system tab bar, with its plus button, is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` while the current page scrolls. The values match `UITabBarMinimizeBehavior` one to one.

symbols.name: CYLFlatDesignTabBar
symbols.comment: Called when the user taps an item (not when selection changes in code).

symbols.name: tabBarItems
symbols.comment: tabBarItems is same as items， 作用是兼容CYLTabBar，实际效果以items为准。

The `UITabBarAppearance` of the flat design tab bar, like `-[UITabBar standardAppearance]`: one appearance object styles the system tab bar (Liquid Glass and the classic style) and this tab bar alike. Nil (the default) keeps the flat design look and the properties below. `CYLTabBarController` assigns `tabBarController.tabBar.standardAppearance` here when the app has set one, so setting the system tab bar's appearance is enough; assigning this property directly also works. When the selected item has its own `-[CYLFlatDesignTabBarItem standardAppearance]`, the whole bar uses that one while it is selected, as `UITabBar` does. Mapping (UITabBarAppearance → flat design tab bar): backgroundEffect → the background blur (nil: no blur) backgroundColor → the background color backgroundImage → the background image backgroundImageContentMode → the background image's content mode shadowImage → the top shadow line (its own height; tinted by shadowColor if template) shadowColor → a hairline at the top when there is no shadowImage (nil/clear: none) selectionIndicatorImage → drawn behind the selected item selectionIndicatorTintColor → tints the selection indicator image stackedItemPositioning → .centered lays the items out centered; .fill / .automatic fill the width stackedItemWidth → the item width when centered (0: equal share of the width) stackedItemSpacing → the spacing between items when centered stackedLayoutAppearance.normal / .selected / .disabled (UITabBarItemStateAppearance): titleTextAttributes → title font, color and other attributes (they override the item's own) titlePositionAdjustment → the title offset when the item has none (`CYLTabBarController.titlePositionAdjustment` wins, as on the system tab bar) iconColor → the icon tint color (template images) badgeBackgroundColor → the badge background color badgeTextAttributes → the badge font and text color badgePositionAdjustment → the badge center offset Not mapped: inline/compact inline layouts (the flat design bar is always stacked), scroll edge appearances, `badgeTitlePositionAdjustment` and the focused state. Badge values a state does not customize (equal to a new `UITabBarAppearance`) leave the badge's own settings and `CYLBadgeAppearance` in place.

symbols.name: backgroundImage
symbols.comment: The background image will be tiled to fit, even if it was not created via the UIImage resizableImage methods.

symbols.name: shadowImage

symbols.name: useLayoutSafeAreaInsets
symbols.comment: Whether the buttons stay clear of the left/right safe area (e.g. a landscape notch). The background always spans the full width. The one-sided inset of a vertical status bar (the folded iPhone Duo's right-hand status column) is controlled separately by `respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea` (ignored by default).

symbols.name: respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea
symbols.comment: Default is NO. Whether the buttons also stay clear of the inset that a vertical status bar adds on one side, e.g. the 84 pt column on the right of the folded iPhone Duo held upright (iOS 27.1 SDK), where the status bar (Wi-Fi, battery) moves to the trailing edge. NO: that one-sided inset is ignored, so the buttons span the full width and stay centered on screen; the last button can sit partly under the status column. YES: the buttons stay inside the safe area, so the row is shifted left by that column. A vertical status bar is told apart by its inset being on one side only; a landscape notch insets both sides and is still handled by `useLayoutSafeAreaInsets`. Has no effect when `useLayoutSafeAreaInsets` is NO. Only matters while the vertical bar is shown. This property does not switch the vertical bar on or off; that is `CYLTabBarController.allowsVerticalBar` (or a screen's own `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`). With the vertical bar off the status bar is horizontal, there is no one-sided inset, and both values give the same layout.

symbols.name: touchableAreaOutsets
symbols.comment: Issue #91: extra touchable area around the plus button, in points, without changing its frame. Positive values grow it outward (top, left, bottom, right), e.g. `UIEdgeInsetsMake(0, 10, 20, 10)` also takes the 20-pt gap below a raised plus button, so a tap there no longer falls through to the page behind. Default: zero. Every style (classic, Liquid Glass, FlatDesign). Set it in `+plusButton`, or later on the instance.

symbols.name: reportsTapsToDelegate
symbols.comment: Whether a tap on this plus button is reported through `tabBarController:didSelectControl:`. Default YES; set NO when the plus button's own target-action is all you want. Unlike the deprecated `cyl_userInteractionDisabled`, it does not change when the plus button's page is selected, so every tap is reported (e.g. a badge that counts taps). While it is not set, the deprecated `cyl_userInteractionDisabled = YES` still keeps the taps out, as before.

symbols.name: touchableAreaScale
symbols.comment: Scales the touchable area around the plus button's center, before `touchableAreaOutsets`: 1 is the frame (default), 2 doubles its width and height. Values below 1 count as 1, so the area never gets smaller than the button.

symbols.name: showsTouchableArea
symbols.comment: Debugging aid: shows the touchable area as a translucent overlay under the plus button (it takes no touches). Default: NO. Turn it off again to restore the normal look. A superview that clips its bounds also clips the overlay, while the hit test still uses the whole area.

symbols.name: touchableAreaColor

symbols.name: cyl_appliesCenterYOffsetWithoutTitle
symbols.comment: Liquid Glass, a plus button without a title: it replaces the whole tab item and is centered on it, ignoring `+multiplierOfTabBarHeight:` and `+constantOfPlusButtonCenterYOffsetForTabBarHeight:` (NO, the default). Set YES (e.g. in `+plusButton`) to place it with those methods. No effect with a title or in another style, where those methods always apply, nor in the iOS 27.1 vertical bar (iPhone Duo), where the plus button is always centered on its tab.

symbols.name: syncsClassicStylesToAppearance
symbols.comment: Since iOS 13 UIKit ignores the classic styles (`tintColor`, `barTintColor`, `unselectedItemTintColor`, `backgroundImage`, `shadowImage`, `barStyle`) once the tab bar uses `UITabBarAppearance`. When YES (default), each classic setter also writes its value into `standardAppearance` (and `scrollEdgeAppearance` when there is one), so both ways of styling work together; only a value that changed is written. Not with Liquid Glass, where the system draws the bar. Set NO to keep UIKit's own behavior.

symbols.name: context
symbols.comment: This can be left unset; the default is CYLTabBarController. If set, please implement the `+[CYLPlusButton tabBarContext]` method in CYLPlusButton and ensure consistency. If neither is implemented, the default is CYLTabBarController for both.

symbols.name: cyl_itemEdgeInsets
symbols.comment: Space kept free at the two ends of the classic tab bar: the tab buttons (and the plus button) are laid out between `left` (the leading end, mirrored in right-to-left layouts) and `right` (the trailing end); `top` and `bottom` are not used. Default `UIEdgeInsetsZero` (the layout is exactly as before). Works with and without a plus button, and together with centered positioning (docs/Tab-Item-Positioning.md). Liquid Glass and FlatDesign are not affected. ((CYLTabBar *)tabBarController.tabBar).cyl_itemEdgeInsets = UIEdgeInsetsMake(0, 16, 0, 16);

symbols.name: CYLTabBarConfigurationFormat
symbols.comment: The key-value file formats a tab bar configuration can be written in (see `-[CYLTabBarController initWithConfiguration:]`). Every format gives the same dictionary: its keys are the configuration and item keys (`CYLTabBarControllerContext`, `CYLTabBarItemTitle`, ...).

symbols.name: CYLTabBarConfigurationErrorDomain
symbols.comment: Error domain of the configuration parser and loaders.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarConfigurationMaximumLength
symbols.comment: The largest file or response read: 5 MB.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarConfigurationMaximumDepth
symbols.comment: The deepest nesting accepted: 64 levels, far more than a configuration needs, far less than overflows the stack.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarConfigurationParser
symbols.comment: Reads key-value configuration files into dictionaries, in every `CYLTabBarConfigurationFormat`. Foundation only, no UIKit: the values stay strings, numbers, booleans, arrays and dictionaries; `CYLTabBarController` turns them into insets, offsets, sizes, URLs and images (see `-[CYLTabBarController initWithConfiguration:]`). Binary Protocol Buffers use the built-in schema of Configurations/cyl_tabbar_configuration.proto. Text formats are read as UTF-8. YAML, TOML, INI, .properties and XML give unquoted `true` / `false` as booleans and numbers as NSNumber; YAML and TOML support the common subset used for configuration (no anchors, tags or multi-line block scalars in YAML; no dates in TOML).

symbols.name: cyl_tabButtonTapAnimationType

symbols.name: cyl_defaultTabButtonAnimation

symbols.name: cyl_tabButtonTapSoundEnabled
symbols.comment: Plays a sound on every reported tap of a tab button or the plus button: right before `-tabBarController:didSelectControl:` is called, together with the tap animation, so in the same cases (a tap, a repeated tap on the selected tab, a swipe, a change of `selectedIndex` in code; not a tap refused by the login check). Default NO. The sound is `cyl_tabButtonTapSoundURL`, or the system keyboard click when it is nil. Like any system sound, it follows the ring/silent switch and the system volume. Ported from the `PlaySound` / `NSObject (Sound)` code suggested in the issue (JobsKits/JobsTabbarItemLottie); here the sound is created once and released when it changes.

symbols.name: cyl_tabButtonTapSoundURL

symbols.name: cyl_tabButtonHapticFeedbackEnabled
symbols.comment: Plays an impact haptic on every reported tap of a tab button or the plus button, with the tap sound (see `cyl_tabButtonTapSoundEnabled` for when). Default NO. Ported from the issue's `+feedbackGenerator` (`UIImpactFeedbackGenerator`). Only devices with a Taptic Engine vibrate; the simulator does not.

symbols.name: cyl_tabButtonHapticFeedbackStyle
symbols.comment: The strength of `cyl_tabButtonHapticFeedbackEnabled`. Default `UIImpactFeedbackStyleMedium`, as in the issue.

symbols.name: cyl_didLongPressControlBlock
symbols.comment: Called on a long press on a tab button or the plus button, before `-tabBarController:didLongPressControl:`. With either of them, a long press no longer selects the tab when the finger lifts.

symbols.name: cyl_tabButtonLongPressMinimumDuration
symbols.comment: How long a press lasts before it is a long press. Default 0.5 s, at least 0.1 s. The same value as `cyl_tabBarItemLongPressDuration` (issue #152): one recognizer serves both long press APIs.

symbols.name: cyl_swipeToSwitchTabEnabled
symbols.comment: Swipe the page left for the next tab and right for the previous one, with a slide animation. Default NO. The tab under the plus button is skipped when the plus button has no child view controller. The switch goes through `-tabBarController:shouldSelectViewController:` and the login check (issue #19), like a tap. It starts only on a horizontal swipe, when the selected tab's navigation stack is at its root, and not on a horizontally scrolling scroll view, so the back gesture and carousels keep working.

symbols.name: CYLViewDidLayoutSubViewsBlock

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemTitle
symbols.comment: Optional per-tab colors (UIColor), in `tabBarItemsAttributes` (or `-updateTabBarItemAtIndex:attributes:`). See docs/Tab-Item-Colors.md. - `CYLTabBarItemTitleColor` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitleColor`: the title color, unselected / selected. - `CYLTabBarItemIconColor` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedIconColor`: the icon tint, unselected / selected. Only template images are tinted (`UIImageRenderingModeAlwaysTemplate`, SF Symbols); image names are drawn as original. - `CYLTabBarItemSelectedBackgroundColor`: fills the selected tab (classic tab bar and FlatDesign; Liquid Glass draws its own selection). Title and icon colors need iOS 13+ (`UITabBarAppearance`) and are ignored on iOS 12. Classic and Liquid Glass: the colors are written into the tab's own `UITabBarItem.standardAppearance` (and `scrollEdgeAppearance` on iOS 15+), a copy of the tab bar's appearance that is rebuilt when that one changes, as for `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment`; an appearance you installed on the item is kept as the base. FlatDesign: the flat item's title attributes and `selectedBackgroundColor`.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitle
symbols.comment: Optional title (NSString) shown while the tab is selected, like JD's "Home" tab that reads "Refresh" when it is selected; the tab shows `CYLTabBarItemTitle` again when another tab is selected. Works in every style (classic, Liquid Glass, FlatDesign). Pair it with `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` (or a Lottie animation, which replays on a re-tap) and with the reselect gesture (`cyl_tabBarItemGestureHandler`) to refresh on a second tap. It can be changed in place, like `CYLTabBarItemTitle`, with `-updateTabBarItemAtIndex:attributes:`. See docs/TabBarItem-Selected-Title.md.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemImage
symbols.comment: `CYLTabBarItemImage` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` (and the dark keys below) take an image name or a UIImage. A name is the prepared form, recommended for most cases: it is rendered as original (the icon keeps its colors) and its dark image is loaded for you. A UIImage is used as it is: an image from `imageNamed:` has the `Automatic` rendering mode, which a tab bar tints as a template, so icons turn into one-color silhouettes unless you call `imageWithRenderingMode:UIImageRenderingModeAlwaysOriginal` first.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemDarkImage
symbols.comment: Optional dark images for `CYLTabBarItemImage` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage`, as a name or a UIImage. The tab then shows them where the interface style is dark (system setting or `overrideUserInterfaceStyle`) and switches by itself. Not needed when the image has a Dark appearance in the asset catalog or a "<name>_dark" image exists (`UIImage.cyl_darkImageNameSuffix`); when given, they replace those.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemImageURL
symbols.comment: Optional icons from the network, an NSURL or a URL string: unselected (`CYLTabBarItemImageURL`) and selected (`CYLTabBarItemSelectedImageURL`; without it the unselected one is used). `CYLTabBarItemImage` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` stay the default icons and the placeholders: the tab shows them until the download ends, and keeps them when it fails. The downloaded images then replace them, in every style, also over a Lottie icon, through `-setTabBarItemIcon:selectedIcon:size:atIndex:`, drawn with their own colors, a GIF animating. Any source that method takes works too (a file path, a UIImage...). `CYLTabBarItemImageURLSize` (an NSValue of CGSize) sets their size, the placeholder's by default. They are cached in memory and in the sandbox, see `CYLImageCache` to set how long and how much. @{ CYLTabBarItemTitle : @"Home", CYLTabBarItemImage : @"home_normal", // default and placeholder CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage : @"home_selected", CYLTabBarItemImageURL : @"https://example.com/home.png", // replaces them once downloaded CYLTabBarItemSelectedImageURL : @"https://example.com/home_selected.png" }

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLottieDarkURL
symbols.comment: Optional Dark Mode versions of `CYLTabBarLottieURL` / `CYLTabBarLottieFilePath` (an NSURL / a file path). A Lottie animation draws its own colors, so a tab with `CYLTabBarLottieURL` used to stay light in Dark Mode, whatever its images. With one of these, the tab shows the dark animation where the interface style is dark (system setting or `overrideUserInterfaceStyle`), and switches by itself, keeping the selected tab's state. CYLTabBarLottieURL : [NSURL fileURLWithPath:[[NSBundle mainBundle] pathForResource:@"tab_home" ofType:@"json"]], CYLTabBarLottieDarkURL : [NSURL fileURLWithPath:[[NSBundle mainBundle] pathForResource:@"tab_home_dark" ofType:@"json"]],

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLottieDarkColors
symbols.comment: One Lottie file for both styles: an NSDictionary of keypath -> UIColor, the colors used where the interface style is dark. They are set with Lottie's official value providers (`setValueProvider(_:keypath:)` with a `ColorValueProvider`), which both rendering engines support, and removed in light mode, so the animation shows its own colors again. Switching keeps the view and its progress. Keypaths use Lottie's syntax: layer, group and item names joined by ".", with "*" for one name and "**" for any number (see `logHierarchyKeypaths()`): CYLTabBarLottieDarkColors : @{ @"Icon_Shop_Normal.**.Color" : [UIColor colorWithWhite:0.78 alpha:1], // gray strokes, lighter @"Icon_Shop_Active_Main.**.Color" : [UIColor colorWithRed:0.15 green:0.39 blue:0.16 alpha:1], }, Lottie 2.x (`CYLTabBarController/LottieObjectiveC`) ignores it; use `CYLTabBarLottieDarkFilePath` there. A dark file and dark colors can be combined: the colors then apply to the dark file.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLottieLoopsWhenUnselected
symbols.comment: Optional, per tab (an NSNumber BOOL, default NO): the tab's Lottie animation (`CYLTabBarLottieURL` / `CYLTabBarLottieFilePath`) loops while the tab is NOT selected, inviting a tap, and pauses while it is selected, instead of playing once on selection. Lottie 2.x and 4.x; every style. See docs/Custom-Tab-Bar-Features.md.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarAnimationURL
symbols.comment: Keys for a tab's animation that do not name a library: the file decides which library plays it (".json" Lottie, ".pag" PAG, or the file type of any library added later, see `CYLTabBarItemAnimatorRegistry`). They work like the Lottie keys, and each library's own keys (`CYLTabBarLottie…`, `CYLTabBarPAG…`) keep working too. - `CYLTabBarAnimationURL` (NSURL) / `CYLTabBarAnimationFilePath` (NSString): the file; the URL wins. - `CYLTabBarAnimationSize`: the view size, an NSValue of CGSize (default: the icon placeholder size). - `CYLTabBarAnimationDarkURL` / `CYLTabBarAnimationDarkFilePath`: the Dark Mode version (#442). - `CYLTabBarAnimationDarkColors`: keypath -> UIColor for Dark Mode, for libraries that support it (Lottie 4.x).

symbols.name: CYLTabBarAnimationColors
symbols.comment: `CYLTabBarAnimationColors`: keypath -> UIColor applied in every appearance, for libraries that support color overrides (Lottie 4.x, Rive). A theme color (`+[UIColor cyl_colorWithThemeProvider:]`) is resolved again on every theme change, so the animation follows the skin; `CYLTabBarAnimationDarkColors` is added on top of it in Dark Mode.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarAnimationOption
symbols.comment: Options of a tab animation, for `CYLTabBarAnimationURLWithOptions()`. Each library declares the options it reads in its own subspec (e.g. `CYLTabBarAnimationOptionRiveArtboard` in the `Rive` subspec); Core only carries them.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemIdentifier
symbols.comment: Optional identifier of a tab (an NSString), like a tag. When tabs come and go (e.g. the server hides the second or third one), `selectedIndex` no longer tells which tab it is; the identifier does. Read it as `viewController.cyl_tabBarItemIdentifier` or `control.cyl_tabBarItemIdentifier` in the delegate methods, and see `CYLTabBarController (CYLTabBarItemIdentifier)` for lookups by identifier. Optional: a tab without one gets a default, its content view controller's class name (a navigation controller's root), e.g. @"CYLHomeViewController", with "_2", "_3"... for the next tabs of the same class; a plus button gets its class name, e.g. @"CYLPlusButtonSubclass" (see `+cyl_defaultTabBarItemIdentifierForClass:`). Class names stay the same when tabs are added or removed and in every language, unlike an index or a title.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerViewControllers
symbols.comment: Keys of a tab bar configuration: one dictionary that holds everything an initializer takes, for `-initWithConfiguration:`, and the same keys in a configuration file (JSON, YAML, plist...) or a downloaded one, see `CYLTabBarController (CYLConfiguration)`. In code the values have their usual types; in a file, strings work for every key (see each key). Missing keys take the defaults of the other initializers. - `CYLTabBarControllerViewControllers`: NSArray<UIViewController *> (code only), matched to the items by index. Without it, each tab's page comes from its page ID, see `CYLTabBarItemPageIdentifier`. - `CYLTabBarControllerTabBarItemsAttributes`: NSArray<NSDictionary *>, the item attributes (`CYLTabBarItemTitle`...). - `CYLTabBarControllerImageInsets`: NSValue of UIEdgeInsets, or "{top, left, bottom, right}", [t, l, b, r] or {top: , left: , bottom: , right: }. Default UIEdgeInsetsZero. - `CYLTabBarControllerTitlePositionAdjustment`: NSValue of UIOffset, or "{horizontal, vertical}", [h, v] or {horizontal: , vertical: }. Default UIOffsetZero. - `CYLTabBarControllerStyleType`: NSNumber of CYLTabBarStyleType, or "default", "system", "flatDesign", "liquidGlass". Default CYLTabBarStyleTypeDefault. - `CYLTabBarControllerContext`: NSString, see `context`. Default nil. - `CYLTabBarControllerPageRegistry`: CYLTabBarPageRegistry or any `CYLTabBarPageProviding` (code only), the page providers of this tab bar controller only, looked up before the shared registry. Lets several tab bars map one page ID to different pages. - `CYLTabBarControllerPageResolver`: CYLTabBarPageProvider block (code only), called for each tab whose page ID is not in `CYLTabBarControllerPageRegistry`, before the shared registry; return nil to go on looking. - `CYLTabBarControllerPageLookupOrder`: NSArray<CYLTabBarPageSource> (or a comma-separated string) of "instance", "resolver", "shared", "automatic": where pages are looked up, in order. Default all four, in that order. - `CYLTabBarControllerAutomaticPageRegistration`: NSNumber (BOOL), or "true" / "false"; NO leaves the classes that adopt `CYLTabBarPage` out of the lookup. Default YES.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerTabBarItemAnimationSpeed
symbols.comment: `CYLTabBarControllerTabBarItemAnimationSpeed`: NSNumber (or a number in a file), the playback speed of every tab animation (`tabBarItemAnimationSpeed`); 1 is the file's own speed. Not set: the default. Invalid (0, negative, NaN, not a number): ignored with a warning.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerPlusButton
symbols.comment: The plus button of a configuration, so a configuration alone (a file, a URL, React Native or Flutter) can show one: - `CYLTabBarControllerPlusButton`: a dictionary with `CYLTabBarItemTitle`, `CYLTabBarItemImage` (an image name, "system:<SF Symbol>" or a UIImage), and optionally `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitle` and `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitleColor` ("#RRGGBB" or a UIColor). It is registered for this configuration's `CYLTabBarControllerContext`, before the tab bar is made: give the configuration its own context so other tab bar controllers keep theirs. The plus button sits in the middle, so give an even number of tabs. With a title, the title lines up with the tab titles (`+alignsTitleWithTabBarItemTitles`). Not a dictionary: ignored with a warning. - `CYLTabBarControllerPlusButtonAction`: a block `void (^)(CYLPlusButton *plusButton)` (code only), run when the plus button is tapped.

symbols.name: CYLPlusButtonBackgroundImage
symbols.comment: More keys of the `CYLTabBarControllerPlusButton` dictionary, for the layouts the `CYLPlusButtonSubclassing` methods give in code (Example-PAG, Example-Rive): - `CYLPlusButtonBackgroundImage`: an image drawn as the button's background, the title on it (an image name, a path or a UIImage); the button takes the image's size. Use it instead of `CYLTabBarItemImage` for a title on a picture. - `CYLTabBarItemTitleColor` ("#RRGGBB" or a UIColor) and `CYLTabBarItemTitleFont` (as for tabs): the title's look. - `CYLPlusButtonIndexInTabBar`: NSNumber, its place among the tabs (`+indexOfPlusButtonInTabBar`). Default: the middle. - `CYLPlusButtonCenterYMultiplier` / `CYLPlusButtonCenterYOffset`: NSNumbers, its vertical center (`+multiplierOfTabBarHeight:` / `+constantOfPlusButtonCenterYOffsetForTabBarHeight:`). - `CYLPlusButtonAlignsTitle`: BOOL, whether the title lines up with the tab titles (`+alignsTitleWithTabBarItemTitles`). Default: YES with a title and no background image. - `CYLPlusButtonKeepsTitleVisible`: BOOL, the title stays visible on Liquid Glass (`cyl_keepShowingPlusButtonLabel`). - `CYLPlusButtonShowsSelection`: BOOL, Liquid Glass shows the selection (the lens and the selected title) under the plus button while its own page is selected, as an app returning YES from `-tabBarController:shouldShowPlatterLiquidLensViewForControl:` (the Objective-C example). Default: NO. Android always shows it. - `CYLPlusButtonSize`: the button's size ("{55, 80}", [55, 80] or an NSValue of CGSize), as a subclass sets its bounds. Default: the size of its image and title. - `CYLPlusButtonImageSize`: the size its images are drawn at, aspect fit (same formats), e.g. for an image downloaded at 512 px, as the example draws a skin's image in the old image's frame. Default: the images' own size. - `CYLTabBarItemIdentifier`: its identifier (`+tabBarItemIdentifier`). - `CYLTabBarItemPageIdentifier`: the plus button selects a page of its own, found like a tab's page (the configuration's resolver, registry or the shared registry; `+plusChildViewController`).

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerUserInterfaceStyle
symbols.comment: Interaction and appearance keys of a configuration: - `CYLTabBarControllerUserInterfaceStyle`: "light", "dark" or "system" (default): the tab bar controller's `overrideUserInterfaceStyle` (iOS 13+), e.g. dark glass for white icons. - `CYLTabBarControllerTabButtonTapAnimation`: "none", "scale", "zoomIn", "bounce", "bounceWithFireworks", "rotation", "flip" or "fume" (`cyl_tabButtonTapAnimationType`). - `CYLTabBarControllerSwipeToSwitchTab`: BOOL, swiping on the tab bar switches tabs (`cyl_swipeToSwitchTabEnabled`). - `CYLTabBarControllerLoginRequiredTabBarItemIdentifiers`: the identifiers (`CYLTabBarItemIdentifier`) of the tabs that need login (`cyl_loginRequiredTabBarItemIdentifiers`, issue #19), e.g. ["message", "mine"]; an array of strings or a comma-separated string. - `CYLTabBarControllerUnloadsUnselectedViewsOnMemoryWarning`: BOOL, a memory warning unloads the views of the tabs that are not selected (`unloadsUnselectedViewsOnMemoryWarning`, issue #426). - `CYLTabBarControllerKeepsLoadedTabBarItemIdentifiers`: the identifiers of the tabs a memory warning never unloads (`cyl_keepsLoadedTabBarItemIdentifiers`), what overriding `-shouldUnloadViewOfViewController:` does in code; an array of strings or a comma-separated string.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerThemes
symbols.comment: Skins in a configuration (see docs/Configuration-File.md, "Skins"; the named values follow QMUI's skins): - `CYLTabBarControllerThemes`: the skins, by identifier: a dictionary {"light": {values}, "dark": {values}}, or a list of {`CYLTabBarThemeIdentifier`: "light", `CYLTabBarThemeValues`: {values}} (the Protobuf form). The values are named: a tab value "@name" (e.g. `CYLTabBarItemTitleColor`: "@accent", `CYLTabBarItemImage`: "@homeIcon") takes the value `name` of the current skin, and changes when the skin changes; "@@" starts a literal "@". The names `CYLTabBarBackgroundColor`, `CYLTabBarShadowColor`, `CYLTabBarItemTitleColor`, `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitleColor`, `CYLTabBarItemIconColor`, `CYLTabBarItemSelectedIconColor`, `CYLTabBarItemTitleFont` and `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitleFont` style the whole tab bar. A name a skin does not give comes from the skin of `CYLTabBarControllerThemeIdentifier`. - `CYLTabBarControllerThemeIdentifier`: the skin used first, and the one others fall back to. Default: the first identifier in alphabetical order. - `CYLTabBarControllerDarkThemeIdentifier`: the skin used in Dark Mode (iOS 13+): the tab bar then follows the system appearance, unless the manager already has its own `identifierForTrait`. - `CYLTabBarControllerThemeManagerName`: the `CYLThemeManager` the skins are registered with (default: the tab bar controller's `cyl_themeManager`, so the app's other views and skin menus see them too). Each skin becomes a `CYLTabBarConfigurationTheme` (a `CYLTabBarTheme`) of that manager; switch with `manager.currentThemeIdentifier = @"dark"`. A skin chosen before (persisted, or set by the app) is kept.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerLocalization
symbols.comment: Configuration key: localized texts (docs/Configuration-File.md, "Localization"). YES (or "true"), the name of a strings table, or a dictionary with `CYLTabBarLocalizationTableName`, `CYLTabBarLocalizationPath` and `CYLTabBarLocalizationBundleName`. With it, every `CYLTabBarItemTitle`, `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitle`, `CYLTabBarItemAccessibilityLabel` and `CYLTabBarItemAccessibilityHint` in the configuration (tabs, the plus button, skins) is a key looked up in `{language}.lproj/{table}.strings` for the library's language (`CYLLocalizationLanguage()`); a key with no translation stays as it is, as with `NSLocalizedString`. Android reads the same files, so one configuration and its tables serve every platform.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerConfigurationRoute
symbols.comment: Configuration key: a resource route (`CYLResourceRoute`, docs/Resource-Routes.md) to a configuration file, built into the app or in its sandbox, e.g. "bundle:Configurations?name=tabbar" or "sandbox:Caches/tabbar?name=tabbar&theme=dark". The file's keys are read first, then the other keys of this configuration win over them, so code (or React Native and Flutter, which send a dictionary) can change a few values of a file. A route that matches no file is logged and ignored. Android reads the same key.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarControllerManifestRoute
symbols.comment: Configuration key: a resource route to a tab bar manifest (`CYLTabBarManifest`, docs/Configuration-Manifest.md). The manifest's configuration (`-[CYLTabBarManifest configuration]`) is read first, then the other keys win over it; React Native's `manifestRoute` prop and Flutter's `manifestRoute` parameter write it. A route that is not a manifest this app may use (platform, app version, time) is logged and ignored. Android reads the same key.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLocalizationTableName
symbols.comment: The strings table, without ".strings" (default "Localizable").

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLocalizationPath
symbols.comment: The folder that holds the `{language}.lproj` folders, always in the app (never in this library), as a location route (docs/Configuration-Localization.md): "bundle:<path>" (the app's resources), "sandbox:Documents/…", "sandbox:Caches/…" or "sandbox:tmp/…" (tables downloaded at run time; the same names on Android), a "file:" URL, an absolute path, "~/…" (the app's home folder), or a path relative to the configuration file's folder (to the app's resources when the configuration did not come from a file). Takes precedence over `CYLTabBarLocalizationBundleName`.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLocalizationBundleName
symbols.comment: A resource bundle in the app ("Texts" or "Texts.bundle"; Android: a folder in the assets); default the main bundle (Android: the assets root).

symbols.name: CYLTabBarThemeIdentifier
symbols.comment: The identifier of a skin in the list form of `CYLTabBarControllerThemes`.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarThemeValues
symbols.comment: The named values of a skin in the list form of `CYLTabBarControllerThemes`.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarBackgroundColor
symbols.comment: Skin value name: the background color of the whole tab bar.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarShadowColor
symbols.comment: Skin value name: the separator line on top of the tab bar.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarBackgroundImage
symbols.comment: Skin value name: an image behind the whole tab bar (`UITabBarAppearance.backgroundImage`): a name, "system:<name>" or a path.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarShadowImage
symbols.comment: Skin value name: the image of the line on top of the tab bar (`UITabBarAppearance.shadowImage`).

symbols.name: CYLTabBarStackedItemPositioning
symbols.comment: Skin value name: how the items share the width (`stackedItemPositioning`): "centered", "fill" or "automatic".

symbols.name: CYLTabBarStackedItemWidth
symbols.comment: Skin value name: the width of each item when centered, in points (`stackedItemWidth`; 0: an equal share).

symbols.name: CYLTabBarStackedItemSpacing
symbols.comment: Skin value name: the space between centered items, in points (`stackedItemSpacing`).

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemPageIdentifier
symbols.comment: Item keys of the pages and of remote configurations (see docs/Tab-Page-Registry.md): - `CYLTabBarItemPageIdentifier`: NSString, the cross-platform ID of the tab's page, e.g. "home"; iOS and Android register what it creates (see `CYLTabBarPageRegistry`). Missing or "": `CYLTabBarItemIdentifier` is used. A tab whose page is not found is skipped. Used only when `CYLTabBarControllerViewControllers` is not given. - `CYLTabBarItemPageParameters`: NSDictionary, passed to the page provider in the tab's attributes, e.g. {url: "https://..."} for two tabs that show the same web page class. - `CYLTabBarItemPlatforms`: NSArray<NSString *> or a comma-separated NSString, e.g. ["ios", "android"]; the tab is left out on iOS unless the list contains "ios". Missing: every platform. - `CYLTabBarItemMinimumAppVersion`: NSString, e.g. "2.3.0"; the tab is left out when the app's CFBundleShortVersionString is lower. With view controllers from code, a left-out tab takes its view controller out with it. In a file, image keys (`CYLTabBarItemImage`, `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` and the dark ones) also take "system:<SF Symbol name>" (iOS 13+), e.g. "system:house.fill"; Lottie URL keys take an http(s) URL, a path or a file name in the main bundle; `CYLTabBarItemImageURLSize` / `CYLTabBarLottieSize` take "{width, height}"; `CYLTabBarLottieDarkColors` takes "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA" colors.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarAnimationOptions
symbols.comment: `CYLTabBarAnimationOptions`: the options of the tab's animation as a dictionary, option name -> string, for configurations (files, URLs or dictionaries). `-initWithConfiguration:` writes them into the fragment of the tab's animation URLs (`CYLTabBarAnimationURL`, a library's URL key, and their Dark Mode versions) with `CYLTabBarAnimationURLWithOptions()`; a tab that only has a file path gets a file URL with the options, so the same options can be written in a file as in code. The names are the option strings, e.g. "artboard", "stateMachine", "input" for Rive (`CYLTabBarAnimationOptionRive…`). Not a dictionary: ignored with a warning. {"CYLTabBarAnimationURL": "icons.riv", "CYLTabBarAnimationOptions": {"artboard": "HOME", "input": "active"}}

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemTitleColor
symbols.comment: Optional per-tab colors (UIColor), in `tabBarItemsAttributes` (or `-updateTabBarItemAtIndex:attributes:`). See docs/Tab-Item-Colors.md. - `CYLTabBarItemTitleColor` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitleColor`: the title color, unselected / selected. - `CYLTabBarItemIconColor` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedIconColor`: the icon tint, unselected / selected. Only template images are tinted (`UIImageRenderingModeAlwaysTemplate`, SF Symbols); image names are drawn as original. - `CYLTabBarItemSelectedBackgroundColor`: fills the selected tab (classic tab bar and FlatDesign; Liquid Glass draws its own selection). Title and icon colors need iOS 13+ (`UITabBarAppearance`) and are ignored on iOS 12. Classic and Liquid Glass: the colors are written into the tab's own `UITabBarItem.standardAppearance` (and `scrollEdgeAppearance` on iOS 15+), a copy of the tab bar's appearance that is rebuilt when that one changes, as for `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment`; an appearance you installed on the item is kept as the base. FlatDesign: the flat item's title attributes and `selectedBackgroundColor`.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemIconRenderingMode
symbols.comment: FIX: issue #787 (and #159, #465, #588). How a tab's icon takes its colors, after Kongzue Tabbar's `noDyeing` and `focusColor` / `normalColor`: - `CYLTabBarItemIconRenderingMode` (a tab) / `CYLTabBarControllerIconRenderingMode` (every tab without its own): "template": the icon is tinted, so one image serves both states (no selected image needed): unselected with `CYLTabBarItemIconColor`, selected with `CYLTabBarItemSelectedIconColor`, else the tab bar's tint colors. "original": the icon keeps its own colors, even when an icon color is set (the fix for gray icons, #465 / #588). "automatic" (default): as before: on iOS image names keep their colors and template images (SF Symbols) are tinted; on Android an icon is tinted when it has an icon color. - `CYLTabBarControllerIconColor` / `CYLTabBarControllerSelectedIconColor`: the icon colors of every tab without its own ("#RRGGBB" in a file, or a UIColor), like Kongzue Tabbar's `normalColor` / `focusColor` for icons. iOS and Android (`CYLConstants`, same keys); React Native and Flutter are a TODO in docs/Tab-Item-Colors.md.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemBackgroundColor
symbols.comment: Optional background of the tab while NOT selected (UIColor), the counterpart of `CYLTabBarItemSelectedBackgroundColor`, which falls back to it when not set. Classic tab bar and FlatDesign, as the selected one. With `itemSpacing` (and no item width), the tab bar shows through the gaps as separators. See docs/Tab-Item-Colors.md.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemTitleFont
symbols.comment: Optional per-tab title fonts (UIFont), unselected / selected; the selected state uses the unselected font unless it has its own. Applied like the colors above (iOS 13+), also in FlatDesign. A larger font for one tab, or a bold title only while selected. See docs/Tab-Item-Colors.md.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemAccessibilityIdentifier
symbols.comment: Accessibility of a tab, for VoiceOver and UI tests (`app.tabBars.buttons["home"]`). See docs/Tab-Accessibility.md. - By default every tab gets an `accessibilityIdentifier`: its `CYLTabBarItemIdentifier` (or the default one, its content view controller's class name); the plus button gets its own identifier the same way. An identifier the app set itself is never replaced. - `CYLTabBarItemAccessibilityIdentifier`, `CYLTabBarItemAccessibilityLabel`, `CYLTabBarItemAccessibilityHint` (NSString) in `tabBarItemsAttributes` set them explicitly; without a label VoiceOver reads the title as before. Classic and Liquid Glass: written on the tab's UITabBarItem, which UIKit's tab button reads. FlatDesign: written on the flat tab button. Applied on layout, so a reload or an in-place update is picked up.

symbols.name: CYLTabbarItemsCount
symbols.comment: These globals hold what was written LAST, by whichever tab bar controller or plus button wrote last. The library no longer lays out with them: with several tab bar controllers they overwrote each other (a tab bar with 5 items was laid out with the 3 of the one pushed after it, issues #414, #489). Each tab bar keeps its own values: `-[UIView cyl_tabbarItemsCount]`, `-[UIView cyl_tabBarItemWidth]`, `-[UIView cyl_plusButtonIndex]`, `-[UIView cyl_plusButtonWidth]` (see UIView+CYLTabBarControllerExtention.h) and `-[CYLTabBarController tabBarHeight]`. With one tab bar controller they are what they always were.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLoginCompletion
symbols.comment: Called once a login started by `-cyl_loginHandler` / `-tabBarController:presentLoginForViewController:completion:` ends: YES when the user logged in (the tab they tapped is then selected), NO when they cancelled.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarLoginStateDidChangeNotification
symbols.comment: Posted when `-[CYLTabBarController cyl_loggedIn]` is set; `object` is the tab bar controller it was set on.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarReselectBehavior
symbols.comment: What the library does when the user taps the tab that is already selected (a "reselect"). See `-[CYLTabBarController cyl_reselectBehavior]` and docs/Tab-Reselect.md. - PopToRoot: a navigation controller with pushed pages pops back to its root page. - ScrollToTop: the page's scroll view scrolls back to the top. - PopToRootThenScrollToTop: both, as the system apps do: the first tap pops, the next one (already at the root) scrolls to the top.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemGesture
symbols.comment: Gestures on a tab button or the plus button, reported by `cyl_tabBarItemGestureHandler` and `-tabBarController:didRecognizeTabBarItemGesture:control:viewController:`, in every style (classic, Liquid Glass, FlatDesign). See `CYLTabBarController (CYLTabBarItemGesture)` and docs/TabBarItem-Gestures.md. - Reselect: a tap on the tab that is already selected (e.g. scroll to the top). - DoubleTap: two taps on the same tab within `cyl_tabBarItemDoubleTapInterval` (e.g. refresh, as Weibo does). The second tap is also a Reselect, reported first. - LongPress: a long press began on the tab (e.g. a menu). The tab is still selected when the finger lifts.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarItemGestureHandler
symbols.comment: The block of `cyl_tabBarItemGestureHandler`. `control` is the tab button or the plus button; `viewController` is its tab's view controller (the plus child view controller for the plus button), nil for a plus button without one.

symbols.name: CYLTabBarController

symbols.name: titlePositionAdjustment
symbols.comment: The title offset of every tab. A tab's own `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment` takes precedence over it. Settable at runtime: setting it re-applies the offset to the tabs already added and lays them out again. On iOS 13+ UIKit ignores `-[UITabBarItem titlePositionAdjustment]` once the tab bar uses `UITabBarAppearance` (e.g. after `tabBar.standardAppearance = ...`), so the offset is also written into a copy of the tab bar's `standardAppearance` (and `scrollEdgeAppearance` on iOS 15+) installed on each tab with an offset. Changes the app makes to the tab bar's appearance later are picked up on the next layout. `UIOffsetZero` leaves the tabs untouched, so an offset set through the appearance proxy or `UITabBarAppearance` still applies (issue #583). Works for all tab bar styles: the classic system tab bar, Liquid Glass (iOS 26+) and FlatDesign.

symbols.name: automaticallyAdjustsImageOnlyTabs
symbols.comment: Whether image-only tabs (tabs without a title) are adjusted automatically. Default is YES. When the first tab button has no title label, the classic tab bar measures once how far the image has to move to be vertically centered (`-[CYLTabBar tabImageViewDefaultOffset]`), then, for every tab whose item has no title, sets `imageInsets` to that offset and moves the empty title out of the way (`titlePositionAdjustment`). A value of the app is never replaced: tabs with a title, an item with its own `imageInsets` or `titlePositionAdjustment` (set on the item or with `CYLTabBarItemImageInsets` / `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment`), and a non-zero controller-level `imageInsets` / `titlePositionAdjustment` are left as they are. Set it to NO to turn the adjustment off and lay out the tabs yourself: the tab bar stops measuring, and the values it had already written are restored. Set it before the tab bar is laid out (in `-init…` or `-viewDidLoad`) to avoid seeing the icons move once. Classic tab bar only (including Liquid Glass); FlatDesign never adjusts tabs.

symbols.name: noNeedUIDesignCompatibility
symbols.comment: Setting NO means flat design. This property is the code alternative to the UI compatibility mode and only takes effect on iOS26+. Since the name of the UI compatibility mode is obscure, the more elegant and intuitive way is to set CYLTabBarStyleType, which internally sets this property to decide whether flat design is used. @return means CYLTabBarStyleType == CYLTabBarStyleTypeFlatDesign if return NO, means CYLTabBarStyleType == CYLTabBarStyleTypeLiquidGlass if return YES; @attention better switch to property CYLTabBarStyleType

symbols.name: allowsVerticalBar
symbols.comment: Whether the system may show the bars in the vertical bar: a column on the leading or trailing edge that iOS 27.1 uses on some devices, such as the folded iPhone Duo. Defaults to NO. - NO: CYLTabBarController returns `UIVerticalBarBehaviorDisabled` from `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`, so the tab bar stays at the bottom and the status bar stays horizontal. Exception (issue #672): a screen that overrides `preferredVerticalBarBehavior` itself (the selected view controller, or the top view controller of a selected navigation controller) still decides for itself, e.g. return `UIVerticalBarBehaviorAutomatic` to opt in. - YES: the system default behaviour, as in 1.99.65 and earlier. `UITabBarController` passes the choice to the selected view controller, so each screen can still opt out by overriding `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`. This is a convenience switch for UIKit's `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`; a subclass may override that property directly instead. Changes apply immediately: the setter calls `setNeedsUpdateOfVerticalBarConfiguration`. Not related to `tabBarController.sidebar.preferredPlacement` / `sidebar.isAvailable` (iOS 27): those choose between the tab bar and an iPad-style sidebar when there is room for one (regular width) and need the `UITab` API; the vertical bar is used in compact width, where the sidebar is not available. Status with YES: Liquid Glass style verified on the iPhone Duo simulator (layout, Lottie icons, badges, plus button, re-tap, long press and drag). FlatDesign style verified on the iPhone Duo simulator: the status bar moves to the trailing column and the FlatDesign bar stays at the bottom with its items centered across the full width (see `CYLFlatDesignTabBar.respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea`). Folded iPhone Duo, FlatDesign, vertical status bar with centered items: tabBarController.allowsVerticalBar = YES; // respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea keeps its default NO No effect below iOS 27.1 or when built with an SDK older than iOS 27.1.

symbols.name: cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior
symbols.comment: How the tab bar reacts when the current page scrolls. Default `CYLTabBarMinimizeBehaviorAutomatic`. - Liquid Glass on iOS 26+ (every style except FlatDesign): sets the native `UITabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior`. The system shrinks the tab bar and picks the scroll view; choose it with `-[UIViewController setContentScrollView:forEdge:]` when a page has several. - FlatDesign: hides the tab bar with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` when the selected page (the top page of a navigation controller) scrolls, and shows it again on the opposite scroll, when the page scrolls back to the top (OnScrollDown), and when another tab or page appears. A tab bar hidden by your own `-setTabBarHidden:` is left hidden. The scroll view is the page's `-contentScrollViewForEdge:NSDirectionalRectEdgeBottom`, otherwise the first scroll view in its view hierarchy. - Classic tab bar (every style except FlatDesign on iOS 25 and earlier, and on iOS 26 in UI compatibility mode): the system tab bar, with its plus button, is hidden with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` when the selected page scrolls, and shown on the opposite scroll, at the top (OnScrollDown) and when another tab or page appears (animated by UIKit on iOS 18 and later, as FlatDesign before iOS 18). Pages pushed with `hidesBottomBarWhenPushed` are left to UIKit, and a tab bar at the top (not at the bottom) is never hidden. FlatDesign and the classic tab bar hide through the same public `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` you can call yourself; a tab bar you hid with it stays hidden. Can be set at any time, before or after the view loads. When it comes back (issue #13, as in the Facebook app): the bar hides only while the user drags down through content; it comes back at once, in every style, on background / foreground switches, a call, any system or in-app alert, a modal page, another key window, a push notification, a push or pop, and a memory warning, and hides again only on a new drag. Robust by design: a whitelist, not a list of events. The bar stays hidden only inside a hide session, started by the user scrolling down and bound to its context (page, tab, scroll view, window); anything else, also this controller's appear / disappear / size change and the keyboard, ends it and shows the bar. See docs/TabBar-Minimize-On-Scroll.md, "When the tab bar hides, and when it comes back". Same switch, Apple's API: on iOS 26+, `tabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior = UITabBarMinimizeBehaviorOnScrollDown` does exactly the same in every style (CYLTabBarController overrides it; both read and write one value). Use this property where iOS 25 and earlier must be supported, since Apple's property does not exist there.

symbols.name: cyl_hidesTabBarOnScroll
symbols.comment: The most direct switch: hide the tab bar while the page scrolls down, show it again when it scrolls back up. Named like UIKit's `hidesBarsOnSwipe` and `hidesBottomBarWhenPushed`, and the same feature as `cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior`, which it reads and writes: tabBarController.cyl_hidesTabBarOnScroll = YES; // == cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior = OnScrollDown tabBarController.cyl_hidesTabBarOnScroll = NO; // == cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior = Never What YES does in each style: - Liquid Glass (iOS 26+): calls Apple's own `UITabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior = OnScrollDown`; the system minimizes the tab bar. - FlatDesign: the flat tab bar is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` while the page scrolls. - Classic tab bar (iOS 25 and earlier, e.g. iOS 17, and iOS 26 in UI compatibility mode): the system tab bar is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:`, with FlatDesign's animation before iOS 18. The getter is YES while scroll hiding is on in either direction (OnScrollDown or OnScrollUp). Use `cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior` for OnScrollUp or Automatic.

The lookup itself is `+pagesOfTabs:registry:resolver:lookupOrder:keptTabs:skipped:`, which the tab bar controller calls; it can be called directly (e.g. by another container or in tests). symbols.name: CYLResourceRoute
symbols.comment: Resource routes: one string that says where a resource is (a configuration file, a folder of string tables…), built into the app or in its sandbox (e.g. downloaded at run time), the same on iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter (docs/Resource-Routes.md). The prefix decides, in this order: bundle:<path> the app's resources (Android: assets) sandbox:Documents/<path> Documents (Android: filesDir) sandbox:Caches/<path> Library/Caches (Android: cacheDir); sandbox:tmp/<path> the temporary folder sandbox:<path> below the app's home folder (Android: the app's data folder) file:///<path> a local file URL /<path> an absolute path ~/<path> the app's home folder <path> relative to `baseDirectory` (a configuration file's folder), else the app's resources A query picks one file in that folder: `name`, and optionally `theme`, `version` and `format`, for files named `{name}[-{theme}][@{version}].{format}`. Without `version` the highest one wins; without `format` any format the configuration parser reads, preferring JSON, YAML, plist, XML, TOML, then the others: sandbox:Caches/tabbar?name=tabbar&theme=dark&version=2.1&format=json → …/Caches/tabbar/tabbar-dark@2.1.json bundle:Configurations?name=tabbar → the highest tabbar[@version].{json,…} The library never ships these resources: string tables and configuration files belong to the app.

symbols.name: cyl_hideNavigationBarSeparator

symbols.name: cyl_hidesAncestorNavigationBars
symbols.comment: Also hides the navigation bars of the navigation controllers around this one, e.g. when the tab bar controller is pushed onto a navigation controller, so `cyl_navigationBarHidden` hides only the inner bar. They are shown again when no visible page asks for it any more (only the bars hidden this way). Default NO. Applied by the all-in-one `-cyl_viewWillAppearNavigationSetting:` / `-cyl_viewDidDisappearNavigationSetting:`, so by CYLBaseViewController and by `cyl_automaticNavigationSettingEnabled`.

symbols.name: cyl_automaticNavigationSettingEnabled
symbols.comment: The properties above (`cyl_navigationBarHidden`, `cyl_hideNavigationBarSeparator`, `cyl_disablePopGestureRecognizer`, `cyl_hidesAncestorNavigationBars`) only work in subclasses of CYLBaseViewController / CYLBaseTableViewController, or when you call the `-cyl_view...NavigationSetting:` methods yourself. Set this to YES once (e.g. at launch) and they work in any view controller, without inheriting: the library calls those methods after `-viewWillAppear:`, `-viewDidAppear:`, `-viewWillDisappear:` and `-viewDidDisappear:`, for the view controllers that set one of the properties to YES and are inside a navigation controller. The base classes keep working as before and are not called twice. Default NO.

symbols.name: CYLSettingsSection
symbols.comment: Section index of the settings rows at the top of a list: row 0 is the language setting (`-cyl_languageCellForTableView:`), row 1 the memory warning check (`-cyl_memoryWarningCellForTableView:`), row 2 switches the title offset of all tabs (`CYLTabBarController.titlePositionAdjustment`, issue #475), row 3 switches `tabBar.standardAppearance` themes, shared by Liquid Glass and FlatDesign, row 4 toggles the cached login state (`cyl_loggedIn`) and names the tabs that need login (issue #19), row 5 shows the plus button's touchable area and scales it with a slider (issue #91), row 6 selects the next tab by its index without the plus button (`cyl_selectedIndexIgnoringPlusButton`, issue #515), row 7 switches how the tab bar minimizes or hides on scroll (`cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior`, issue #13), row 8 switches the tap animation of the tabs, row 9 turns on the long press of the tabs, row 10 turns on swiping to switch tabs, row 11 shows a subview that responds outside its superview, row 12 loads an image from a bundle, row 13 hides the navigation bar without a base class, row 14 opens the slide transition demo, row 15 switches the tap sound and haptic, row 16 switches the long press duration and double tap interval, row 17 switches to the previous or next tab, row 18 runs the CYLUtils weak associated object and nearest control helpers (issue #535), row 19 pushes a tab bar controller whose plus button gets its image later (loaded, replaced, removed, or a background image), row 20 picks a skin (theme) of the tab bar (`CYLThemeManager`, `CYLTabBarTheme`, issue #216), row 21 lists the scroll hiding simulations in an action sheet (`-cyl_presentScrollHideSimulationMenu`, issue #13), row 22 creates a tab bar controller from a configuration file or URL (`UIViewController+CYLConfigurationDemo.h`), then the simulated failures of configurations, one row each (`-cyl_configurationEdgeCaseCellForTableView:row:`), then the in-place tab item updates (`-cyl_tabBarItemUpdateCellForTableView:row:`): title, icon, network icon, all network icons, all local icons, GIF icon, all titles, replace neighboring tabs.

symbols.name: cyl_tabBarItemIdentifier
symbols.comment: The tab's identifier: `CYLTabBarItemIdentifier` from `tabBarItemsAttributes`, set on the view controller in `viewControllers` and on its content view controller (e.g. a navigation controller's root), or set here directly (e.g. on the plus child view controller, which has no attributes). symbols.name: cyl_tabBarSpacingInViewCoordinator
symbols.comment: How much of the bottom of `self.view` the tab bar covers, in `self.view`'s points: 0 when there is no tab bar, it is hidden, or this page hides it (`hidesBottomBarWhenPushed`). For laying out subviews above the tab bar (e.g. a floating button) in `-viewDidLayoutSubviews` or `-viewWillAppear:`, not in `-viewDidLoad`: it converts frames, so the view must be in a window. Every style: the system tab bar (Liquid Glass, classic) and FlatDesign's own bar.
